# Native script-context insertion evidence

Original OOXML generated by `tools/script_input_fixture.py`; no corpus material
or fonts are included. Sixty-five inputs are inserted between A and B in three
contexts: ordinary, forced cs, and forced rtl (195 cases). Inputs include Latin,
Hebrew, Arabic, digits, punctuation, spaces, tabs, combining marks, directional
controls, emoji, Indic and other scripts, and mixed strings.

`tools/record-script-input.ps1` uses an owned hidden reference-application instance and a temporary
copy. It calls Selection.TypeText once per input, saves a separate native DOCX,
records build and hashes, closes its own document/application and removes only
its temporary input. This is a native object-model insertion experiment, not
physical keyboard input or a claim about every input language/IME. Font/language
changes in the saved XML are retained as evidence; none are copied into an
application font table or used to select a hard-coded font.

The initial model audit found flag mismatches in 91/195 cases: 48 forced-cs,
43 forced-rtl, zero ordinary. The model unconditionally inherits the active
flags. The reference application drops them on Latin insertion, retains rtl on neutrals/numbers in
an RTL context, assigns cs to some complex scripts, and divides mixed input
into separate runs. A blanket clear, a blanket inherit, or a test for any RTL
character in the input is therefore insufficient. Supplementary script and
directional-control observations also rule out simply mapping all Unicode R
characters to w:rtl and all L characters to ordinary formatting.

Reproduce the component comparison with `node tools/audit-script-input.mjs`.
The report compares only cs/rtl flags; font fallback, language selection,
keyboard layout, separate keystrokes and IME behavior remain outside its claim.

The initial results identified the insertion gap. `typedScriptRuns` now splits
insertions by script and writes independent cs/rtl overrides; all 195 original
cases and 100 additional bracket/font controls match native flags. The
active-script import guard remains. Run-level property semantics are
ECMA-376 Part 1 17.3.2.7 (cs) and 17.3.2.30 (rtl); the format chosen for newly
inserted text is application behavior, not a demonstrated OOXML divergence.
The evidence tests check hashes, all inserted text and unchanged neighbor flags,
plus representative native distinctions. They do not assert the current bug
as required behavior and do not claim complete RTL rendering or editing.

The implementation preserves ordinary input and object insertion paths. Model
and browser checks cover raw/native flags, Latin font-size selection during
typing, mixed input, serialization, reopening, undo/redo and long nested input.
Remaining work includes paragraph-break and per-keystroke/IME semantics,
automatic language/fallback-font selection, and styled-source editing coverage
before lifting the package guard.

Validation: both evidence tests pass. The original source passes its three
schema-part checks. Four native ancillary parts pass; native document.xml fails
only on rFonts/@hint="cs". This is the published ST_Hint electronic-schema
omission described in [MS-OE376 2.1.38](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/6855418a-c4fb-4087-aff8-6a6e31c1d0df),
not proof that the reference application violates the written standard. The native output and
validator are left unchanged. The importer already accepts this hint value.
